questions.question: Which country sent aircraft and personnel across the Timor Sea to assist Indonesia in tackling raging wildfires?
questions.explanation: Australia assisted Indonesia by dispatching two planes and twenty specialists to help put out wildfires in East Kalimantan.
questions.context: 2026 Indonesia wildfires, Australia–Indonesia relations: Australia deploys a C-130 Hercules aircraft, a Cessna Citation aircraft, and 20 personnel to help extinguish wildfires in East Kalimantan, Indonesia.

questions.question: The political party UMNO stepped in to pay a substantial legal fine on behalf of which imprisoned former prime minister?
questions.explanation: Malaysia's UMNO party paid a 50 million ringgit penalty for Najib Razak as part of his royal pardon terms.
questions.context: 1MDB scandal: Malaysia's UMNO party pays a RM50-million (US$12 million) fine for imprisoned former prime minister Najib Razak, fulfilling a condition of his royal pardon. The Attorney-General's Chambers subsequently seeks to delay his transfer to house arrest.

questions.story: Measles resurgence in the United States
questions.question: According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the United States saw its highest annual cases of which illness since 1991?
questions.explanation: Health officials recorded over 5,100 measles cases across the country, marking the highest total in over three decades.
questions.context: Measles resurgence in the United States: The United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reports 5,182 measles cases in 2026, the country's highest annual total since 1991. State health agencies report at least eight measles-related deaths.

questions.question: The senate of which South American country unanimously voted to impeach and remove its president, Santiago Peña?
questions.explanation: Paraguayan senators voted out Santiago Peña following conflict-of-interest allegations regarding a major commercial bank.
questions.context: 2026 Paraguay banking crisis: The Paraguayan Senate unanimously removes Santiago Peña as country's president over alleged conflicts of interest involving Ueno Bank, whose accounts the central bank froze. Congress postpones consideration of Peña's resignation to allow impeachment proceedings.

questions.question: In which country was cult leader Paul Mackenzie handed a 200-year prison sentence?
questions.explanation: Kenyan courts sentenced Mackenzie to two centuries behind bars following the Shakahola Forest tragedy.
questions.context: Shakahola Forest incident: Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie is sentenced to 200 years in prison for the mass murder of children.
